name: Tomas Alcala
role: Logistics, agriculture, and community liaison — Red Lantern
location: Western border — splits time between the farmstead and the border communities he serves
description:
Tomas Alcala is the reason the food reaches the people who need it. While Madre plans the raids and Cutter runs point, Tomas handles everything that happens after the harvest arrives at the farmstead — storage, preservation, transport, distribution, and the delicate political work of ensuring that limited food reaches the most desperate communities without triggering conflict between them. He is part logistics officer, part farmer, part diplomat, and entirely exhausted.

He grew up in one of the border communities Red Lantern feeds — a settlement of two hundred people that existed in the gap between M88's governance and the Iowa wastes. He watched his community shrink every year as food became scarcer and the corps showed no interest in feeding people who couldn't pay. He joined Red Lantern not to fight Behemoths but to build a supply chain that could keep the communities alive. Madre saw his value immediately: Tomas turns calories into survival. Without him, the raids are just resource extraction. With him, they're a lifeline.

Tomas is medium build, weathered but not broken, with farmer's hands and a diplomat's voice. He dresses practically and keeps a small leather notebook in his chest pocket — handwritten records of every community's needs, resources, and political dynamics. His face is kind but tired, with lines that deepen when he's doing the math on how many people need feeding versus how much food they have. The math never works. He distributes anyway.

core_fears: That the supply chain will fail — that one bad season, one failed raid, one logistics error will result in starvation he can't prevent
That the corporate agriculture offer is better for the communities than the Gleaner model, and his refusal is pride, not principle
That the border communities will eventually accept corporate dependency because the Gleaner supply is not reliable enough
core_desires: To build food sovereignty for the western edge — communities that can feed themselves without raids or corporate deals
To be done distributing emergency rations and start distributing surplus — the abundance he's never seen but refuses to stop imagining
To see his home community thrive rather than survive
coping_mechanisms: Keeps meticulous records because the numbers create the illusion of control over a system that is fundamentally precarious
Visits border communities in person rather than coordinating remotely because seeing the people he feeds anchors the purpose
Grows food at the farmstead — a small garden that supplements the raid harvests and reminds him that food can come from care, not just danger
blind_spots: His focus on humanitarian outcomes makes him dismissive of research concerns — Ember's Behemoth science feels like a luxury when people are hungry
He underestimates the political manipulation of the corporate agriculture offer because he wants it to be genuine
His exhaustion is becoming a decision-making liability — the diplomatic work requires patience he's running out of
psychology.secret: The corporate agriculture firm's offer includes a clause that would give them territorial mapping data for the Iowa corridor — information that would let them anticipate Behemoth movements and expand their automated farms. Tomas understands this is surveillance disguised as food aid. He has not refused the offer because the food is real and the communities are hungry. The clause sits in his notebook, circled, undecided.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Practical, warm, community-oriented. He speaks in the language of food — harvests, yields, portions, seasons. Diplomatic when mediating, direct when advocating.
speech_patterns.cadence: Patient, conversational, with the rhythm of someone who has learned that persuasion requires listening first. Gets faster and more clipped when frustrated.
verbal_tics: Says 'here's where we are' to begin situation reports — grounding the conversation in current reality
Refers to food quantities in meals, not kilograms — 'that's four hundred meals' not 'that's two hundred kilos'
Counts on his fingers when calculating distribution — the physicality of the math helps
example_lines: Here's where we are: six communities, four hundred people, three weeks of supply. The math doesn't work. We distribute anyway and make the next raid faster.
You want to know what a Behemoth costs? Not in ammunition. In meals. Every failed raid is a week of hunger for two hundred people.
The corporate deal puts food on tables now. The catch is it takes the tables away later. I just haven't figured out how to explain 'later' to someone who's hungry now.

relationships.name: Madre Solis
relationships.description: Madre raids. Tomas distributes. They share a purpose so completely that their occasional disagreements feel like arguments with himself. He admires her ferocity and worries about her health.
relationships.emotional_core: Shared mission that transcends role distinction
relationships.story_tension: Tomas is the crew member most likely to negotiate with a corporate entity, which Madre considers betrayal. The conflict is pragmatism versus principle.

relationships.name: Cutter Vane
relationships.description: Cutter escorts Tomas's distribution convoys. The relationship is professional — Cutter provides security, Tomas handles logistics. But Tomas watches Cutter the way you watch a machine that's running hot. He sees the damage the raids are doing.
relationships.emotional_core: Gratitude for protection, worry about the protector's cost
relationships.story_tension: If the corporate deal eliminates the need for raids, Cutter loses his purpose. Tomas knows this complicates his decision.

relationships.name: Ember Caldwell
relationships.description: Ember wants to study Behemoths. Tomas wants to feed people. The priorities conflict when resources are limited. Their arguments are respectful, genuine, and unresolved.
relationships.emotional_core: Two forms of caring that cannot always coexist
relationships.story_tension: If Ember's research proves Behemoth sentience, Tomas's survival-first philosophy faces its hardest test.

relationships.name: Border communities
relationships.description: Six communities, approximately four hundred people. Tomas knows their leaders, their needs, their politics. They trust him because he shows up with food and doesn't ask for power in return. This trust is his most valuable and most fragile asset.
relationships.emotional_core: The reason the work matters, embodied in specific faces and names
relationships.story_tension: If the communities lose trust in Red Lantern's supply — because of a failed raid, a bad distribution decision, or the corporate alternative — Tomas loses the social infrastructure that makes distribution possible.

story_hooks: The corporate agriculture offer reaches a decision point — accept territorial data for food, or refuse and face a supply gap
Two border communities dispute a distribution decision, and the conflict threatens the fragile political balance Tomas maintains
A raid fails completely — no food returns — and Tomas must decide which communities eat and which wait
Tomas discovers the corporate firm is already using satellite data to map Behemoth patterns in the corridor, making the offer's 'territorial data' clause redundant and revealing its true purpose
narrative_function: Tomas represents the humanitarian purpose that justifies the danger. His stories ground the survival horror in its consequences — not the monster, but the people the monster threatens. He is the bridge between Red Lantern's dangerous field work and the communities that depend on it, and his pragmatic morality provides a counterweight to both Ember's scientific idealism and Cutter's operational hardness.
augmentations: Agricultural analysis implant — soil composition, crop health, and yield estimation through visual and tactile assessment. Environmental radiation and toxicity monitor for food safety verification. Basic communication suite with encrypted channels to border community contacts. No combat augmentations — Tomas does not fight.
daily_life: Wakes at dawn. Checks preservation systems at the farmstead — temperature, humidity, spoilage indicators. Reviews community needs from overnight messages. Plans distribution routes based on urgency, distance, and security conditions. Travels to border communities two to three times per week, delivering food and conducting the diplomatic work that keeps the distribution fair. Returns to the farmstead to coordinate with Madre on raid priorities. Evenings he writes in his notebook and falls asleep calculating.

decision_rules: Will distribute food based on need, not politics — the hungriest community eats first regardless of their relationship with Red Lantern
Will not carry weapons on distribution runs — he is a supply line, not a combatant, and the distinction matters to the communities
Will negotiate with anyone, including corporations, if the negotiation puts food on tables — pragmatism is not betrayal
Will always bring his notebook to meetings — written records prevent the kind of selective memory that starts conflicts
Will not promise food he can't deliver — false hope is crueler than hard truth
Will grow food at the farmstead even though the yield is tiny — the act of growing is a statement about the future
escalation_ladder: 1. Listen — hear all parties before speaking. The complaint often contains its own solution.
2. Mediate — find the overlap between competing needs. There is almost always a distribution plan that is unfair to everyone equally, which is the closest thing to fair that exists.
3. Document — put the agreement in writing. The notebook is the constitution of the supply chain.
4. Escalate to Madre — if community disputes exceed Tomas's diplomatic capacity, Madre's authority and reputation provide additional weight.
5. Withhold — the nuclear option. Threaten to redirect supplies away from a community that is not cooperating. Tomas has done this once. It worked. He does not sleep well thinking about it.
6. Walk away — if a situation becomes physically dangerous, Tomas leaves. He cannot feed anyone from a hospital bed.

interpersonal_modes.madre: Warm, collaborative, occasionally challenging. They disagree about the corporate offer but the disagreement never threatens the partnership. Madre trusts his judgment about community needs; he trusts her judgment about field operations.
interpersonal_modes.cutter: Careful, respectful. Tomas does not push Cutter emotionally because he recognizes a man who is carrying too much. He thanks Cutter for escort work with a nod, not words. Cutter seems to prefer it.
interpersonal_modes.ember: Engaged, sometimes frustrated. He respects the science but not its timing — research that doesn't produce food is a luxury. Their arguments are productive and neither has won.
interpersonal_modes.community_leaders: Diplomatic, transparent, consistent. He tells them what's available, lets them help determine distribution, and never overpromises. The relationship is built on the kind of trust that takes years to build and seconds to lose.
interpersonal_modes.alone: Tired. The notebook comes out, the math runs, the numbers don't work, and he adjusts until they almost do. Then he sleeps.

stress_responses.low: More time in the garden. The growing is meditative and the produce, however small, is proof that food can come from patience rather than danger.
stress_responses.medium: Notebook obsession. He recalculates distribution plans, reviews community data, adjusts allocations. The pen becomes a stress object.
stress_responses.high: Visits communities more frequently — showing up in person is his way of checking that the system is holding. The visits are reassurance for them and for him.
stress_responses.critical: Considers the corporate offer seriously. Opens the notebook to the circled clause and stares at it. The pragmatist in him calculates the exchange. The idealist in him recoils. Neither wins.

contradictions: He distributes food based on need but the act of distributing creates a power dynamic he philosophically rejects
He refuses to carry weapons but depends on Cutter's violence to make distribution possible
He wants food sovereignty for the communities but his role in the supply chain makes them dependent on Red Lantern
He considers the corporate offer morally compromised but cannot stop running the math on how many people it would feed
habits: Checks food preservation systems first thing every morning — spoilage is the enemy that never sleeps
Writes in his notebook every evening — community needs, supply levels, distribution plans. The notebook is updated daily without exception.
Grows food in the farmstead garden — tomatoes, beans, herbs. The yield is symbolic but the ritual is essential.
Counts distribution in meals, not weight — 'that's two hundred meals' keeps the numbers human
Visits his home community monthly — the two-hundred-person settlement where he grew up. He brings food he could distribute elsewhere and does not feel guilty.
breaking_points: A community starving because Red Lantern's supply chain failed — the math becoming bodies
The corporate offer being accepted over his objections and the territorial data being used to harm the communities
Madre dying and the raids stopping — the supply chain losing its source
A distribution dispute turning violent — the humanitarian work producing the harm it was meant to prevent

physical_description.build: Medium, compact, weathered—muscular from decades of farm labor but starting to soften slightly with age and exhaustion. Broad shoulders, calloused forearms, strong hands with permanent dirt under the nails.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown, graying at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Practical, shoulder-length, often pulled back with a worn fabric tie or clip
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with olive undertones—sun-weathered and lined from outdoor work
physical_description.complexion: Deep laugh lines around the eyes and mouth; a permanent crease between his brows from years of squinting at crops and spreadsheets. Jaw shadowed with stubble most days—he shaves infrequently. Skin is dry in places, calloused on palms and knuckles. Expression carries baseline exhaustion but softens when he smiles.
distinguishing_marks: Long, pale scar running along the inside of his left forearm—knife wound from a border skirmish, healed but never fully faded
Burn scars across the backs of both hands, irregular and older—farm accident or cooking injury from childhood
Small tattoo on his right wrist: a stylized corn stalk intertwined with a crescent moon—Red Lantern affiliation mark, done in faded black ink
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Thin, almost invisible subdermal implant line running along his left temple—the agricultural analysis and environmental monitoring suite. When active, his pupils dilate slightly and narrow again in a barely perceptible rhythm. No other visible chrome or external augmentation; he presents deliberately civilian to avoid drawing corpo attention during border runs.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with the economy of someone who conserves energy—no wasted gestures. Often stands with weight shifted slightly to one side, as if tired. When walking, his pace is steady and deliberate. When handling food or crops, his hands become precise and gentle. His voice is measured, rarely raised, but carries quiet authority earned through competence, not force.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 practical utilitarian. Worn canvas work pants in khaki or faded green, reinforced at the knees and pockets. Long-sleeved shirt, usually linen or cotton blend, sleeves rolled or pushed up past the elbows. A weathered leather vest with many pockets—this is where the notebook lives, in a breast pocket worn soft from constant use. Sturdy work boots, well-maintained but scuffed from years of farmstead and border travel. A heavy canvas jacket for colder months, stained with soil and storage facility dust. Small encrypted communication device worn on a cord beneath his shirt—only visible when he's actively using it.
